ambiguities.text: The specification recommends including chainId and nonce in dataToSign but does not mandate it
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume implementations SHOULD include chainId and nonce for replay protection. Security analysis should consider cases where they are omitted.

ambiguities.text: The term 'verifier' and 'validator' are used interchangeably without clear distinction
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume 'verifier' and 'validator' refer to the same concept: the contract/address that will verify the signature.

ambiguities.text: Error handling behavior not specified for invalid parameters or signature failures
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume standard JSON-RPC error codes apply. Invalid parameters should return error, not a malformed signature.

implicit_assumptions.description: Users will verify the validator address displayed by the wallet before approving signature requests
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Users may sign messages for malicious validators, enabling phishing or unauthorized actions

implicit_assumptions.description: Wallets will honestly display the validator address and data to sign without manipulation
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Malicious wallets could trick users into signing for unintended validators

implicit_assumptions.description: An attacker cannot forge ECDSA signatures without the private key
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Signature forgery would compromise the entire signing mechanism

implicit_assumptions.description: The dApp requesting signature is the legitimate application the user intends to interact with
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Malicious dApps could request signatures for fraudulent purposes, with valid validator address but malicious data
